title: Base change and etale descent of closed subsets proper over the base
statement: Let $p:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $C\subseteq T$ be a closed subset. A closed subset is proper over its base when its reduced induced closed subscheme is proper [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (1) For any $v:S'\to S$, let $T'=T\times_SS'$ with projection $v_T:T'\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $C$ is proper over $S$, then $v_T^{-1}(C)$ is proper over $S'$. (2) If $\{v_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism] and every inverse image $C_i\subseteq T\times_SS_i$ is proper over $S_i$, then $C$ is proper over $S$. No quasi-compactness assumption is made on $p$, $S$, or the members of the etale covering.

source.place: Tag 0CYP (coherent-lemma-base-change-closed-proper-over-base); Tag 0F4J (descent-lemma-descending-property-proper-over-base), applied to an etale covering, refined over affine opens to finite affine etale subcovers

proof.text: Write $i:Z=C_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow T$ for the reduced induced closed subscheme. Its underlying set is $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](2), and if $C$ is proper over $S$, this means that $p\circ i$ is proper by [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. For any $v:S\prime\to S$, put $Z\prime=Z\times_SS\prime$. By the fibre-product universal property, $Z\prime\cong Z\times_T(T\times_SS\prime)$; thus $Z\prime\to T\prime$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Its underlying set is $v_T^{-1}(C)$, as follows. Cover $T$ by affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $v_T^{-1}(U)$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The reduced-structure statement gives $Z\times_TU=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ with $C\cap U=V(I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] the restriction of $Z\times_TT\prime$ over $V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}((R/I)\otimes_RB)$. The ring map $(R/I)\otimes_RB\to B/IB$, $\bar r\otimes b\mapsto rb\bmod IB$, is an isomorphism: its inverse sends $b\bmod IB$ to $1\otimes b$, which kills $IB$ since $1\otimes rb=\bar r\otimes b=0$ for $r\in I$. Consequently the image over $V$ consists of primes of $B$ containing $IB$; a prime contains $IB$ exactly when its contraction to $R$ contains $I$, which is exactly membership in $v_T^{-1}(C)\cap V$. These affine opens cover $T\prime$, proving the asserted equality. This argument also identifies the supports for all the covering base changes below.

The ambient projection $p\prime:T\prime\to S\prime$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. If $C$ is proper over $S$, then $Z\prime\to S\prime$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1) to the closed subscheme $Z\prime\subset T\prime$ constructed in step 1 shows that its underlying subset $v_T^{-1}(C)$ is proper over $S\prime$. This proves (1); no assertion that $Z\prime$ is reduced is needed.

For (2), each $S_i\to S$ is an object of the small etale site of $S$, and their jointly surjective family covers its identity object by the covering-family definition in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] makes it an fpqc covering. For each $i$ let $Z_i=Z\times_SS_i\subset T_i=T\times_SS_i$. Step 1 identifies its underlying closed subset with $C_i$. The ambient $T_i\to S_i$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Since $C_i$ is proper by hypothesis, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties](1), now in its every-closed-structure direction, shows that $Z_i\to S_i$ is proper. Reducedness of $Z_i$ is neither asserted nor required.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-morphism-fpqc-descent] to the morphism $Z\to S$ and the fpqc covering from step 3. All its pullbacks $Z_i\to S_i$ are proper by that step, so $Z\to S$ is proper. By [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] this says that $C$ is proper over $S$, proving (2). The argument uses fpqc covering families, not quasi-compactness of $p$, $S$, or the covering members.
